videos.title: PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 3 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 3 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026 Check out all the best shots from the third round of the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship, featuring Scottie Scheffler, Sungjae Im, Jordan Spieth and Sam Burns, among others.

The 2026 FedExCup Playoffs begin this week at TPC Southwind with the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as 69 of the top 70 players in the standings begin their pursuit of the season-ending title. With only the top 50 advancing to next week’s BMW Championship, the opening playoff event carries immediate significance for players fighting to keep their seasons alive. Rory McIlroy returns to action after missing last year’s event and makes his first start since The Open Championship. McIlroy enters the Playoffs outside the top 10 for the first time since 2021 but remains in position to challenge for a fourth FedExCup title. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler leads the standings despite having just one victory this season, with five runner-up finishes and a T2 at the 3M Open in his most recent start. Defending FedExCup champion Tommy Fleetwood returns at No. 9 in the standings, while Justin Rose looks to defend his FedEx St. Jude Championship title after winning last year’s event in a playoff. No player has successfully defended the tournament since it became part of the FedExCup Playoffs in 2007. Ryan Fox also returns for his first PGA TOUR start since winning The Open Championship, while stars including Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup look to carry their strong 2026 seasons into the postseason. The battle for the top 50 adds another layer of drama, with players such as Max Homa, Sungjae Im, Jordan Spieth, Shane Lowry and rookie Jackson Koivun all needing strong weeks to advance to the BMW Championship. Koivun, who only secured the 70th and final playoff spot after winning the 3M Open, faces the biggest climb, needing at least a T7 to have a chance of reaching the top 50. With 750 FedExCup points available and no cut during the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship sets the tone for the final push toward East Lake. Only 50 players will advance to the BMW Championship, making Memphis the first major pressure point of the 2026 postseason.

videos.title: OpenAI Revealed Astra. 6 Days Later, It's Locked Away
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Revealed Astra. 6 Days Later, It's Locked Away Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
OpenAI revealed Astra as one of its most advanced upcoming AI models. Just six days later, the company halted internal activities involving Astra that didn’t meet stricter security controls after evaluations raised concerns about potentially critical cyber capabilities.

So what exactly did Astra do?

In this video, we break down what OpenAI has actually confirmed about Astra, the mathematical and theoretical computer science results that put the model on the radar, why its cybersecurity capabilities triggered additional safeguards, and what this could mean for the future of frontier AI models.

Astra reportedly contributed to ten advances across areas including quantum complexity, lattice cryptography, coding theory, and extremal combinatorics. But the bigger story may be what happened next.

OpenAI said evaluations showed significant advances in agentic coding and cybersecurity and concluded that it could not rule out critical cyber capabilities under its Preparedness Framework.

That distinction matters.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to action after a three-week break with the penultimate event of the Closing Swing at the Danish Golf Championship. Great Northern will host its first DP World Tour event this week, following in the footsteps of Himmerland, Silkeborg Ry Golf Club, Lübker Golf Resort and Furesø Golf Klub in staging this event. videos.title: Busting The Ankle Collapse Myth In Hockey
videos.summary_source_text:
Busting The Ankle Collapse Myth In Hockey The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Hank Green did nothing wrong
videos.summary_source_text:
Hank Green did nothing wrong Hank Green got “caught” using AI… and I genuinely don’t think he did anything wrong.

The whole controversy started because Hank said “I appreciate the pushback” in a video — a phrase people thought sounded suspiciously like ChatGPT.

That led to Hank explaining that while he doesn’t use AI to write his scripts, he DOES use it to help find research papers that he then reads himself.

And somehow, that turned into a much bigger debate about whether creators should be using AI at all.

I actually understand why people care. If you watch someone specifically for THEIR opinions, perspective, and commentary, you probably don’t want those things outsourced to an LLM.

But using AI as a better research tool or dumping your own messy thoughts into it and asking it to help organize them feels like a completely valid use-case to me.

I also think people need to give creators a little more grace here.

Creators are often working under a ton of pressure to constantly research, write, film, edit, publish, and somehow keep doing it over and over again while also having families, businesses, careers, and lives outside of what you see on camera.

Of course they're going to look for ways to make that process more optimized and sustainable.

Curious what your take on this is...

videos.summary_source_text:
The Putting Habit I Wish I Learned Years Ago STRUGGLING WITH DISTANCE CONTROL OR MISSING SHORT PUTTS?

If your putting stroke suddenly feels unreliable, you’re three-putting too often or you’ve lost confidence over those 3–6 foot putts, this lesson will help. I’m going to show you the simple 3-step putting routine I use to improve distance control, hole more putts and get my confidence back on the greens.

Putting has always been one of the strongest parts of my game, but recently something changed. My distance control disappeared on fast greens, I started missing short putts and suddenly I was three-putting two or three times a round.

Whenever that happens, I go back to a simple system a mentor taught me many years ago.

And it works every time.

In this video, I explain:

• The simple putting setup check that allows your putter to swing naturally
• Why your head and body position can cause pulls without you realising
• How centre-face contact dramatically improves putting distance control
• A simple drill to help you consistently strike the middle of the putter
• Why I always aim the putter BEFORE setting my body
• The putting routine I use to stop thinking technically on the golf course
• How visualisation can help you develop better pace and feel
• My “guessing game” drill for learning the speed of unfamiliar greens
• How to practise short breaking putts so you become more instinctive under pressure

The goal isn’t to create a complicated putting stroke.

It’s the opposite.

I want you to build a simple setup, learn to strike the centre of the putter face and then trust your instincts when you’re standing over the ball.

Because great putting isn’t about consciously controlling how far the putter moves back and through.

Eventually it should feel as natural as throwing a ball to someone.

If you’re deficient in bile, try taking 200 mg of ox bile after a meal.

TUDCA doesn’t break down fat, so ox bile is better suited for supporting fat digestion. Try taking 250 mg of TUDCA on an empty stomach twice per day.

How’s this for an almighty RWD drag race?!

videos.title: This Mobility Test Explains Your Swing  #golfswing #golftips
videos.summary_source_text:
This Mobility Test Explains Your Swing  #golfswing #golftips This simple 90/90 mobility test gives you a clear look at how your right arm should function in the golf swing. From a 5-iron posture, lift and rotate the arm until it matches your spine angle—if you can’t get there, your backswing is likely compensating by standing up or losing posture. That compensation often leads to poor ball striking and inconsistent contact. Your swing should reflect what your body can actually do, even if that means a shorter backswing.

Hindi - 14.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 2 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 2 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026 Check out all the best shots from the second round of the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship, featuring Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy, Jordan Spieth and Hideki Matsuyama, among others.

The 2026 FedExCup Playoffs begin this week at TPC Southwind with the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as 69 of the top 70 players in the standings begin their pursuit of the season-ending title. With only the top 50 advancing to next week’s BMW Championship, the opening playoff event carries immediate significance for players fighting to keep their seasons alive. Rory McIlroy returns to action after missing last year’s event and makes his first start since The Open Championship. McIlroy enters the Playoffs outside the top 10 for the first time since 2021 but remains in position to challenge for a fourth FedExCup title. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler leads the standings despite having just one victory this season, with five runner-up finishes and a T2 at the 3M Open in his most recent start. Defending FedExCup champion Tommy Fleetwood returns at No. 9 in the standings, while Justin Rose looks to defend his FedEx St. Jude Championship title after winning last year’s event in a playoff. No player has successfully defended the tournament since it became part of the FedExCup Playoffs in 2007. Ryan Fox also returns for his first PGA TOUR start since winning The Open Championship, while stars including Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup look to carry their strong 2026 seasons into the postseason. The battle for the top 50 adds another layer of drama, with players such as Max Homa, Sungjae Im, Jordan Spieth, Shane Lowry and rookie Jackson Koivun all needing strong weeks to advance to the BMW Championship. Koivun, who only secured the 70th and final playoff spot after winning the 3M Open, faces the biggest climb, needing at least a T7 to have a chance of reaching the top 50. With 750 FedExCup points available and no cut during the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship sets the tone for the final push toward East Lake. Only 50 players will advance to the BMW Championship, making Memphis the first major pressure point of the 2026 postseason.

videos.title: Scottie Scheffler TIES COURSE RECORD to take lead! | Round 2 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
Scottie Scheffler TIES COURSE RECORD to take lead! | Round 2 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026 In the second round of the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship, Scottie Scheffler ties the course record, shooting 9-under 61 to get to 11-under par, taking a three-shot lead into the weekend.

The 2026 FedExCup Playoffs begin this week at TPC Southwind with the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as 69 of the top 70 players in the standings begin their pursuit of the season-ending title. With only the top 50 advancing to next week’s BMW Championship, the opening playoff event carries immediate significance for players fighting to keep their seasons alive. Rory McIlroy returns to action after missing last year’s event and makes his first start since The Open Championship. McIlroy enters the Playoffs outside the top 10 for the first time since 2021 but remains in position to challenge for a fourth FedExCup title. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler leads the standings despite having just one victory this season, with five runner-up finishes and a T2 at the 3M Open in his most recent start. Defending FedExCup champion Tommy Fleetwood returns at No. 9 in the standings, while Justin Rose looks to defend his FedEx St. Jude Championship title after winning last year’s event in a playoff. No player has successfully defended the tournament since it became part of the FedExCup Playoffs in 2007. Ryan Fox also returns for his first PGA TOUR start since winning The Open Championship, while stars including Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup look to carry their strong 2026 seasons into the postseason. The battle for the top 50 adds another layer of drama, with players such as Max Homa, Sungjae Im, Jordan Spieth, Shane Lowry and rookie Jackson Koivun all needing strong weeks to advance to the BMW Championship. Koivun, who only secured the 70th and final playoff spot after winning the 3M Open, faces the biggest climb, needing at least a T7 to have a chance of reaching the top 50. With 750 FedExCup points available and no cut during the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship sets the tone for the final push toward East Lake. Only 50 players will advance to the BMW Championship, making Memphis the first major pressure point of the 2026 postseason.

Episode 54: Defensive Discourse | Tri-State Hockey Podcast Jonny Lazarus, Arthur Staple, and Mike Rupp are back for Episode 54 of the Tri-State Hockey Podcast to debate some of the biggest questions surrounding the Rangers, Islanders, Devils, and the Metropolitan Division heading into the 2026-27 NHL season. 

The guys react to the NHL Network’s Top 20 defensemen rankings, including Adam Fox being left outside the top 10, Matthew Schaefer landing at No. 7, Lane Hutson’s rise, Evan Bouchard, Charlie McAvoy, and more. 

Then, they break down Jason Demers’ early Metro Division predictions and give their own 1-through-8 rankings, debating where the New York Rangers and Islanders stack up against the Carolina Hurricanes, New Jersey Devils, Washington Capitals, Philadelphia Flyers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Columbus Blue Jackets. 

Plus, the crew answers your voicemails, including whether Dylan Larkin could be a fit with the Devils, what Detroit could possibly get back in a trade, whether Quinn Hughes would give New Jersey or Minnesota the better Stanley Cup window, and the latest debate over Hughes’ future with the Wild. 

Could Quinn eventually join Jack and Luke Hughes in New Jersey? Does Minnesota need to get an extension done before the season begins? All that and more on a new Tri-State Hockey Podcast.

Place an alignment stick behind the ball and a head cover just in front — then focus on swinging under the stick and over the head cover. 
You’ll shallow the club naturally, improve your path, and start hitting up on the ball for better launch and distance.

Vilken fond som passar just din bank varierar kolla din egen plattform efter en bred globalindexfond med låg avgift.

videos.title: Gemini 4 Explained: 10 Million Context, Massive Scale & Everything We Know
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4 Explained: 10 Million Context, Massive Scale & Everything We Know https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Google has officially started pre-training Gemini 4 — calling it its “most ambitious” AI training run yet. But almost everything you’ve seen about Gemini 4 specs, benchmarks, parameter counts, pricing, and release dates? That’s where things get messy.

In this video, I separate what Google has ACTUALLY confirmed about Gemini 4 from rumors, speculation, and fake “leaked” spec sheets circulating online.

We’ll break down:

• What Google officially confirmed about Gemini 4
• What Sundar Pichai revealed about the model
• Gemini 4’s possible architecture and scale
• Why there are NO verified Gemini 4 benchmarks yet
• Expected multimodal, coding, context, and agent capabilities
• Gemini 4 vs GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, and Meta’s latest AI
• Possible Gemini 4 release date and pricing
• Google TPU hardware and the massive training run
• Privacy, safety, and the future of AI agents
• What Gemini 4 could actually mean for the AI race

The important distinction: Gemini 4 is real. The exact specifications are not public yet.

Google has confirmed that pre-training has begun, while credible reporting describes Gemini 4 as a significantly larger frontier model. But Google has not published an official parameter count, benchmark report, model card, API pricing, context window, or exact release date.

So instead of repeating rumors, this video looks at the evidence we actually have — and what Google’s roadmap suggests could come next.

Could Gemini 4 become Google’s biggest challenge yet to OpenAI and Anthropic?

Watch to the end for my Gemini 4 release forecast and what I think will matter far more than parameter count.

Subscribe for evidence-based AI news, model comparisons, benchmarks, and deep dives without the fake leaks.

videos.summary_source_text:
Smooth Out Your Tempo With the 1-1000 Drill If your downswing feels rushed, your pressure shift and rotation may be happening at the same time.

Try the 1-1000 drill:
Get to the top → shift pressure into your lead side → count “1-1000” → then rotate and swing through.

That tiny pause helps you separate the pressure shift from the rotation so you can create a smoother transition, better sequencing, and more power through the ball.

The Ball First Board gives you instant feedback on exactly how far you’re shifting, so you can stop guessing and start training the move correctly!

videos.summary_source_text:
This ONE Move Can Flatten Your Stomach The dead bug exercise can tighten loose stomach flab better than sit-ups or crunches! In many cases, that soft look around the midsection isn’t just fat; it can also involve loose, underactivated fascia and connective tissue.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4q7jqUq

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

The dead bug creates tension through the midsection by extending the opposite arm and leg at the same time. This can help activate deeper fascial layers, tighten the waist, improve posture, and support the lower back.

How to do it:
• Lie on your back with your arms straight up and knees bent at 90°
• Slowly extend your right arm behind your head and your left leg straight out
• Return to the starting position and switch sides
• Keep your lower back pressed into the floor the entire time
• Do 10 reps on each side before bed for 2 weeks

videos.summary_source_text:
Why your reverse pivot is costing power  #golfswing #golftips A reverse pivot puts your weight on the front foot in the backswing, making it difficult to generate power or strike the ball cleanly. Without proper loading into the trail side, the downswing sequence breaks down and the club often releases too early. Learning to coil into the trail leg sets up a more efficient shift and leads to better contact and more consistent ball striking.

When faced with gallbladder surgery, most people are told there’s no other option, and the side effects of gallbladder removal aren’t always properly explained. 

The gallbladder is a small sac that stores and concentrates bile, releasing it when you eat to help break down fat. Bile is produced by the liver and is critical for proper nutrient absorption.

Gallbladder stones are one of the main reasons for a cholecystectomy. Gallstones typically form from the crystallization of excess cholesterol. Bile sludge is a precursor to gallstones.

Fat consumption triggers gallbladder contraction and bile release. Low-fat diets are often recommended, but they are not always the best approach for digestive health.

Excess estrogen can increase the risk of gallstones. Insulin resistance can also increase the risk and is often at the root of many gallbladder problems.

The full side effects that can occur after gallbladder removal surgery aren’t always discussed. After gallbladder removal, many people experience problems related to either excess bile or bile deficiency.

Choline is essential for helping prevent gallstones, yet many people don’t get enough. Eggs are one of the best sources of choline.

videos.summary_source_text:
Chris Gotterup gives full breakdown of EVERY shot from his 4-under 66 | Round 1 | FedEx St. Jude Go all-access with Chris Gotterup, who sits 5th in the FedExCup Standings, as he relives his opening round at the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship, breaking down the shots and decisions that shaped his day. In this candid post-round walkthrough, Gotterup offers an honest look at the highs, lows, and mindset of competing on the PGA TOUR. After Round 1, Gotterup sits T6 at the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship.

The 2026 FedExCup Playoffs begin this week at TPC Southwind with the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as 69 of the top 70 players in the standings begin their pursuit of the season-ending title. With only the top 50 advancing to next week’s BMW Championship, the opening playoff event carries immediate significance for players fighting to keep their seasons alive. Rory McIlroy returns to action after missing last year’s event and makes his first start since The Open Championship. McIlroy enters the Playoffs outside the top 10 for the first time since 2021 but remains in position to challenge for a fourth FedExCup title. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler leads the standings despite having just one victory this season, with five runner-up finishes and a T2 at the 3M Open in his most recent start. Defending FedExCup champion Tommy Fleetwood returns at No. 9 in the standings, while Justin Rose looks to defend his FedEx St. Jude Championship title after winning last year’s event in a playoff. No player has successfully defended the tournament since it became part of the FedExCup Playoffs in 2007. Ryan Fox also returns for his first PGA TOUR start since winning The Open Championship, while stars including Cameron Young, Matt Fitzpatrick, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup look to carry their strong 2026 seasons into the postseason. The battle for the top 50 adds another layer of drama, with players such as Max Homa, Sungjae Im, Jordan Spieth, Shane Lowry and rookie Jackson Koivun all needing strong weeks to advance to the BMW Championship. Koivun, who only secured the 70th and final playoff spot after winning the 3M Open, faces the biggest climb, needing at least a T7 to have a chance of reaching the top 50. With 750 FedExCup points available and no cut during the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship sets the tone for the final push toward East Lake. Only 50 players will advance to the BMW Championship, making Memphis the first major pressure point of the 2026 postseason.

13.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 1 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 1 | FedEx St. Jude | 2026 Check out all the best shots from the opening round of the 2026 FedEx St. Jude Championship, featuring Jordan Spieth, Scottie Scheffler, Hideki Matsuyama and Tommy Fleetwood, among others.

The 2026 FedExCup Playoffs begin this week at TPC Southwind with the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as 69 of the top 70 players in the standings begin their pursuit of the season-ending title. With only the top 50 advancing to next week’s BMW Championship, the opening playoff event carries immediate significance for players fighting to keep their seasons alive. Fun Fake Shot Box Drill The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: GPT-5.6 Luna Explained: OpenAI Just Changed Free ChatGPT Forever
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-5.6 Luna Explained: OpenAI Just Changed Free ChatGPT Forever https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI just made one of its biggest changes to free ChatGPT in years.

Free users are reportedly getting GPT-5.6 Luna as their default model with unlimited text chats — removing the message-limit wall that has defined the free ChatGPT experience for years.

But “free” and “unlimited” need some explaining.

Luna isn’t simply OpenAI giving everyone its most powerful model. GPT-5.6 is built around three tiers: Sol, Terra, and Luna. Sol is the flagship, Terra occupies the middle, and Luna is the fast, low-cost model designed for massive-scale everyday usage. What makes this interesting is that Luna reportedly still shares the same enormous 1.05-million-token context window as the higher tiers, while sacrificing some of the reasoning horsepower behind each response.

And the economics behind OpenAI’s decision might be an even bigger story.

Just before expanding Luna to free users, OpenAI slashed its API pricing by 80%, taking Luna to just $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens. That dramatically changes the economics of serving huge numbers of free users — and helps explain how OpenAI can suddenly offer effectively unlimited text conversations without turning every free ChatGPT session into an enormous compute bill.

In this video, I break down exactly what GPT-5.6 Luna is, what OpenAI actually changed for free ChatGPT users, why the pricing story matters, and how Luna fits into the larger GPT-5.6 family.

We also look at how GPT-5.6 stacks up against competing frontier models, why the benchmark picture is more complicated than the launch headlines suggest, and the important distinction between the flagship GPT-5.6 Sol results and what free users are actually getting with Luna.

Then there’s the reaction.

videos.title: This Pullup Just Hits Different
videos.summary_source_text:
This Pullup Just Hits Different Sometimes making an exercise less stable can actually make it more effective, especially when that instability forces muscles to contribute in ways they normally wouldn’t.

This pull-up variation is a perfect example.

By performing the pull-up from a band instead of a completely stable bar, you introduce instability that immediately changes the demands of the exercise. Your back, shoulders, arms, and stabilizing muscles have to work harder to control your body while still producing enough force to complete each rep.

But there’s another reason this variation is worth trying.

The wider grip combined with the changing tension of the band creates a unique challenge for the muscles of the upper back, particularly the teres major.

The teres major is sometimes thought of as one of the lats’ favorite helpers because it assists with many of the same movements, including pulling the upper arm down toward the body. During a traditional pull-up, the lats are obviously doing a significant amount of the work. Change the mechanics, however, and you can alter how much assistance the surrounding muscles have to provide.

That’s exactly what happens here.

As you pull yourself upward, the stretched band creates significant tension and instability. As you approach the bottom of the rep, that band tension begins to decrease. At the same time, the wide hand position limits how much additional arm adduction you can rely on.

The result is a pull-up variation that creates a very different stimulus than simply grabbing a straight bar and performing another set of traditional pull-ups.

That doesn’t mean this exercise should replace regular pull-ups.

If your goal is getting stronger at pull-ups, building your lats, or progressively overloading your back, the standard pull-up should still be one of the foundational exercises in your training. Variations like this are valuable because they allow you to introduce a new challenge without necessarily needing to add more weight.

You’re creating difficulty through instability, positioning, grip width, and changing resistance instead.

This is also why compromised stability isn’t always a bad thing in the gym. If your goal is maximum strength or maximum force production, you generally want a stable environment. But when the goal is creating a different muscular stimulus, strategically introducing instability can force muscles to work in ways they normally wouldn’t.

The key word is strategically.

You don’t need to turn every back exercise into a balancing act. You want enough instability to create the desired training effect without making the movement so unstable that you can’t actually train the muscles you’re targeting.

If you have access to the right setup, give this band pull-up variation a try and pay attention to what you feel through the outer portion of your upper back.

Control every rep, don’t rush the movement, and remember that sometimes changing the stability of an exercise can unlock benefits you simply won’t get from the standard version.

If your goal is getting stronger at pull-ups, building your lats, or progressively overloading your back, the standard pull-up should still be one of the foundational exercises in your training. Variations like this are valuable because they allow you to introduce a new challenge without necessarily needing to add more weight.

You’re creating difficulty through instability, positioning, grip width, and changing resistance instead.

This is also why compromised stability isn’t always a bad thing in the gym. If your goal is maximum strength or maximum force production, you generally want a stable environment. But when the goal is creating a different muscular stimulus, strategically introducing instability can force muscles to work in ways they normally wouldn’t.

The key word is strategically.

You don’t need to turn every back exercise into a balancing act. You want enough instability to create the desired training effect without making the movement so unstable that you can’t actually train the muscles you’re targeting.

If you have access to the right setup, give this band pull-up variation a try and pay attention to what you feel through the outer portion of your upper back.

Control every rep, don’t rush the movement, and remember that sometimes changing the stability of an exercise can unlock benefits you simply won’t get from the standard version.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to action after a three-week break with the penultimate event of the Closing Swing at the Danish Golf Championship. Great Northern will host its first DP World Tour event this week, following in the footsteps of Himmerland, Silkeborg Ry Golf Club, Lübker Golf Resort and Furesø Golf Klub in staging this event. The course is the passion project of Thomas Kirk Kristiansen, a fourth-generation member of the family behind the Lego Group. This event has long been renowned for its bumper crowds and the home fans will have plenty of local talent to cheer for this week. 2023 winner Rasmus Højgaard and fellow Ryder Cupper Thorbjørn Olesen are in action, as is rising star and reigning Australian Open champion Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen. videos.title: OpenAI Is Building a $300 AI “Donut” What Does It Actually Do?
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Is Building a $300 AI “Donut” What Does It Actually Do? https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

OpenAI and Jony Ive’s mysterious AI device may have just gotten its biggest leak yet.

After more than a year of vague descriptions, shifting timelines, and speculation about what this thing actually is, seven separate outlets have now converged on the same reported price range: **$300 to $400**.

But the price isn’t the most interesting part.

The new reporting gives us a much clearer picture of what OpenAI may actually be building: a small, screenless, battery-powered AI companion reportedly shaped like a donut or hockey puck, equipped with cameras, microphones, sensors, speakers, indicator lights, and moving parts designed to give the device something resembling a personality. It’s also reportedly powered by **GPT-Live-1**, a full-duplex voice model capable of listening and speaking at the same time.

And one detail quietly changes the story from the previous leak.

Earlier reports suggested OpenAI’s device might actually move around a room. The newer reporting describes those moving parts as being used for **expression and personality** instead — potentially turning a difficult autonomous robotics problem into something much more realistic to manufacture and ship.

In this video, I break down what actually changed from the last OpenAI hardware leak, why seven outlets reporting the same price band matters, what the reported $300–$400 positioning tells us about OpenAI’s strategy, and why the timing of these leaks deserves more scrutiny than it’s getting.

We also look at the **$6.5 billion OpenAI–Jony Ive hardware deal**, the reported design and GPT-Live-1 integration, the device’s increasingly complicated release timeline, and why OpenAI appears to be positioning this as a second device you use alongside your phone rather than something designed to replace it.

Then there’s the comparison OpenAI probably won’t want following this product into launch: the **Humane AI Pin**.

Humane tried to sell the world on an ambient AI companion and launched at $699. OpenAI’s reported $300–$400 range would make its first device significantly easier to justify — but a lower price doesn’t solve the fundamental problem that killed previous AI hardware: the gap between an incredible demo and something people actually want to use every day.

And there are still major unanswered questions.

There’s no officially confirmed $300–$400 price. No final release date. No confirmed processor or battery life. No confirmed manufacturing partner. And, critically, no published privacy framework explaining how a screenless AI device built around cameras and microphones is supposed to exist inside someone’s home.

So is this finally the leak that tells us what OpenAI and Jony Ive are actually building — or are we looking at an increasingly convincing collection of leaks being mistaken for a finished product?

That distinction matters.

CHAPTERS

01:03 The Number That Just Leaked

14:07 The Verdict

Rushing the downswing with your driver feels exactly like leaving the house late — you don't have enough time and you have to force everything. Eric Cogorno and Golf Digest Top In State instructor Steve Sieracki show that the fix isn't in the downswing at all — it's in building enough time and space in the backswing so the downswing sequences itself. Four moves — trail leg extension, spine extension and tilt, trail arm abduction, and shoulder retraction — give any golfer a longer backswing, a more effortless golf swing, and significantly more driver distance without swinging harder. These easy golf swing tips work especially well for seniors who want to know how to hit driver farther with less effort. If you leave this video without trying the trail arm only drill, you're leaving driver distance and an effortless golf swing on the table.

• Why rushing the downswing is almost always caused by being out of position in the backswing golf swing
• How trail leg extension is the first and most important move for a longer backswing and more driver distance
• The Fosbury flop analogy: spine extension and tilt for a more effortless golf swing with driver
• How trail arm abduction and shoulder retraction contribute to a fuller golf shoulder turn and more turn depth
• The trail arm only drill for isolating backswing depth and feeling all four moves together
• Why Hideki Matsuyama's long slow driver swing rhythm is the feel reference for stopping the rush
• How to hit driver farther by lengthening the backswing — not by swinging harder through the ball
• Easy golf swing tips for seniors who want more driver distance with less effort and less rushing

This Chinese hypercar is a Bugatti killer! The Denza Z offers Bugatti power for Porsche money! 

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Mat’s got his hands on the all-new Denza Z! 

It’s an absolutely insane Chinese hypercar that offers absolutely insane power for a relatively affordable price! 

The question is, can an all-new Chinese brand create a car to compete with the European elite? Let’s take a closer look - starting with the performance stats! 

The Denza Z is an all-electric supercar with a tri-motor set-up - one motor at the front, and two at the rear. The three of these combine to produce an eye-watering 1,600hp, which can propel the Z to 62 mph in around 2 seconds, and it comes with a top speed of 217mph. The edition we have here, with the metal roof, tips the scales at 2,580kg. 

Then let’s check out the design. The Denza Z is available in three variants - Coupe, Convertible & Racing. We’ve got the latter here, which means around the back you’ll find a huge wing, tail lights that remind us of a Bentley, and an absolutely huge carbon fibre diffuser. Along the side you’ll find several vents to help airflow, a carbon fibre roof, and concealed door handles that simply open when you insert your hand into them! Up top, there’s a huge vent in the bonnet, coupled with a massive front splitter packed with a load of real vents. All-in, it’s a proper sporty-looking bit of kit. 

On the inside, the impressive design continues. There’s a layered dash with a 2-tone effect, and there’s fake leather and Alcantara found throughout the cabin. The seats are comfortable with speakers in the headrest, and the large steering wheel comes equipped with several physical buttons. Most features are controlled through the large infotainment screen, and the digital dials offer all the information and stats you need. 

The Coupe edition of the Z costs from £143,000, the Convertible comes in at £159,000, and the Racing edition will set you back £173,000. So you’re offered some incredible power for the same price as a Porsche! The question is: would you choose the Z over a GT3 RS? Let us know in the comments!

videos.title: 12.08.26 - Ep.21 (Part 2)- Identity, Reputation & the Future of Intelligent Financial Infrastructure
videos.summary_source_text:
12.08.26 - Ep.21 (Part 2)- Identity, Reputation & the Future of Intelligent Financial Infrastructure In Episode 21 Part 2 of RIFT Before You Quit, we continue the discussion around prediction markets and explore how prediction, identity, reputation, behavioural analysis and capital allocation could eventually become connected within a single financial ecosystem.

The episode begins by revisiting RIFT's prediction infrastructure and the role prediction markets can play beyond simply forecasting events. Every prediction, trade and decision creates data. Over time, that information can contribute to a broader understanding of participant behaviour, consistency and performance.

This leads to one of the biggest challenges facing decentralized financial systems: Sybil attacks.

A Sybil attack occurs when one individual creates multiple wallets or identities and attempts to make them appear as separate participants. This can be used to manipulate rankings, referral systems, incentives, governance, trading activity and other parts of a decentralized ecosystem.

The episode explains why effective Sybil resistance requires more than simply checking an IP address. Modern systems can consider multiple signals, including device information, network behavior, wallet relationships, transaction history, trading patterns, referral structures and behavioral similarities.

The goal is to distinguish genuine participation from artificially manufactured participation while maintaining fairness and trust within a decentralized environment.

From here, the discussion moves into digital identity and financial reputation.

Traditional financial institutions have always relied on identity, history and behavioural information when assessing risk and allocating capital. As financial activity becomes increasingly digital, a participant's behaviour may become an important part of their financial identity.

The question changes from:

"Who are you?"

to:

"How do you participate?"

Consistency, risk management, trading discipline, prediction accuracy, portfolio behavior and long-term performance could all contribute to a participant's evolving financial reputation.

This concept connects directly to the future vision of the RIFT ecosystem.

A participant could begin with demo trading, learn market mechanics through spot and futures trading, explore Smart Money and mirror wallets, study trading books and capital allocation, and develop probabilistic thinking through prediction markets.

Over time, their participation creates a measurable history.

The proposed journey is:

Learn → Participate → Build Reputation → Demonstrate Consistency → Access Greater Opportunities

The episode then connects this framework to the RIFT Auto Trading Engine, including Alpha Flow, Smart Flow and Micro Flow, before looking toward future prop-trading infrastructure.

Traditional proprietary trading firms already evaluate traders using factors such as profitability, consistency, risk management, capital preservation and execution quality. Future financial infrastructure could make these evaluations increasingly data-driven, using accumulated performance and behavioural history rather than relying solely on isolated results or one-time assessments.

This creates the concept of reputation-driven financial infrastructure, where identity, behaviour, performance and reputation can potentially influence future access to capital.

The episode also emphasizes the importance of education. Prediction markets, artificial intelligence, digital identity, Sybil resistance, risk management and professional execution are not isolated developments. They represent different parts of the broader transformation taking place across modern financial markets.

The RIFT Ecosystem

The episode revisits four core areas of the RIFT ecosystem:

Spot Trading
Futures Trading
Smart Money
Auto Trading Engine

Each serves a different purpose, but together they form part of a connected participant journey.

The next stage is prop trading, where the future direction of RIFT will explore how capital could potentially be allocated according to measurable performance, consistency, reputation and intelligent risk management.

The episode concludes with a broader question:

As financial infrastructure becomes more intelligent, how will the future system decide who should receive access to greater capital?

That question leads directly into the next episode: The Prop Trading Revolution.

Topics ahead include the evolution of prop trading, institutional capital allocation, AI-powered traders, reputation-based funding, dynamic capital scoring, risk-adjusted performance, autonomous prop infrastructure and the future of intelligent capital allocation. videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 12.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Anyone Can Make Amazing Games Now (Easy) I vibe coded a full game sequel using Claude Code and Codex, and it proved something important about AI and game development.

A year ago I built The Librarian, a playable vibe coded game you can still find on GitHub. This time I wanted to see how far AI coding tools have come, and whether one person could build something that actually feels like a real game.

I used Claude Code with Opus 5 for the initial build, then switched to Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol for all the fine-tuning. The result is The Librarian 2, a 3D procedurally generated roguelite with boss enemies, natural disasters, meta progression, and a chaos system. 10,400 lines of code across 33 modules. Zero asset files.

The verdict: game development is far from cooked. But it's also a lot harder than the one-level demos on X make it look.

videos.summary_source_text:
How to Attack More Evasively The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

In this video, I explain what happens during the first 30 minutes after you eat, including digestion, blood sugar, insulin, muscle activity, fullness, reflux, and why staying upright and moving gently can make a difference. Ni förklarar varför det är fel att utvärdera ett beslut baserat på hur det råkade gå, istället för sannolikheterna som fanns kända när beslutet togs. Ett val med bättre förväntad avkastning kan fortfarande gå sämre några år det gör inte valet fel i efterhand.

Detta innehåll är inte individuell investeringsrådgivning. Ett sparande i linje med forskningens rekommendationer har historiskt sett varit framgångsrikt. Alla investeringar innebär risk och kan både öka och minska i värde. Investera inte pengar du inte har råd att förlora. Mer info på rikatillsammans.se.

videos.title: OpenAI Built an AI That Can Hack: And Locked It Behind a Physical Key
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Built an AI That Can Hack: And Locked It Behind a Physical Key Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
OpenAI just shipped GPT-5.6-Cyber — a purpose-built AI model designed for offensive cybersecurity work, with dramatically less refusal friction than a normal GPT-5.6 Sol session.

But the model itself may not be the biggest story.

Access reportedly comes with identity verification, monitoring, approved-use restrictions, legal attestations, and a physical hardware security key requirement. In other words, OpenAI appears to be moving part of the safety system outside the model itself — and into the identity and access layer.

In this video, I break down what GPT-5.6-Cyber actually is, who Daybreak Blue and Daybreak Red are designed for, why the two tiers are easy to misunderstand, what the hardware-key requirement tells us about OpenAI’s risk model, and which capability claims actually have a public receipt behind them.

We also look at the reported V8 vulnerability discovery tied to CVE-2026-15903, the enterprise business behind the launch, GPT-5.6-Cyber’s premium pricing, and the biggest limitation nobody is showing in the demos: controlling who can access a model is not the same thing as controlling what happens to its output afterward.

videos.title: Tusen år av sill – en ny dokumentärserie från Svenska Tidsresor
videos.summary_source_text:
Tusen år av sill – en ny dokumentärserie från Svenska Tidsresor I århundraden har sillen format livet längs våra kuster. När den kom förändrades allt. Fisket växte, människor flyttade, samhällen byggdes och stora förmögenheter skapades. När sillen försvann kunde hela näringar falla samman.

I vår nya dokumentärserie följer vi sillens historia genom århundradena – från de stora medeltida sillmarknaderna och Hansans handel till Bohusläns återkommande sillperioder, fiskelägen, salterier och den industri som så småningom växte fram kring havets kanske viktigaste fisk.

The Tesla Phone rumor is exploding again after new comments surrounding SpaceX, Elon Musk, and Starlink Mobile. But what SpaceX is actually building is much more interesting than another viral Tesla Pi Phone concept.

In this video, we break down what SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell actually said, what Starlink Mobile really is, and why people keep confusing SpaceX’s mobile ambitions with a Tesla smartphone launch.

videos.summary_source_text:
Broncos Preseason Questions, Peyton Watson’s Future & the Rockies’ Arenado Curse | After the Horn The Denver Broncos are heading into their first preseason game, and the biggest question might be who actually needs to play.

On this episode of After the Horn, Woody Paige, Mark Kiszla and Natasha Vukovich break down what they want to see from the Broncos in Atlanta, including the backup quarterback battle, concerns about playing on artificial turf, Davis Webb’s influence on the offense and whether Denver needs to lean more heavily on the running game.

The crew also discusses Sean Payton’s evolution as a head coach, Bo Nix and the Broncos’ Super Bowl window, Deion Sanders’ approach to building chemistry at Colorado, and the questions surrounding CU’s quarterback situation.

Plus, what happens next with Peyton Watson and the Denver Nuggets? Should Watson bet on himself and return on the qualifying offer, or could a trade eventually be the answer?

Finally, the Colorado Rockies’ struggles continue — and after Nolan Arenado’s latest big moment, Woody wonders whether the Rockies are still living under the “Curse of Arenado.”

All that and more on a new episode of After the Horn!

videos.title: Movement Feels Unsafe? This May Be Why
videos.summary_source_text:
Movement Feels Unsafe? This May Be Why Movement can feel guarded, stiff, or hesitant even when you wouldn’t describe yourself as “afraid to move.”

You may notice it as holding your breath, bracing before you move, restricting your range, hesitating, or trying very hard to move the “right” way.

Sometimes these patterns remain even after an injury has healed or you’ve worked on your strength, mobility, or flexibility.

In this video, I’ll help you notice what happens before movement even begins and guide you through a short somatic exploration.

The goal isn’t to push through fear or force your body to relax. It’s to give your nervous system a small, manageable experience of moving with a little less protection — so another possibility can begin to emerge.

Start here: Free Somatic Masterclass

If this way of thinking about your body is new to you, I recommend starting with my free somatic masterclass:

Move More Freely in Your Body
https://taro-iwamoto.thinkific.com/courses/masterclass?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=fear_of_movement_description_masterclass

You’ll experience how gentle somatic movement can help you move from constantly trying to fix your body toward sensing, learning, and moving with more ease.

Want deeper guidance?

If you’ve tried stretching, strengthening, correcting, exercises, or other approaches but still find yourself returning to tension, bracing, pain, or uncertainty in your body, learn about my guided course:

Moving Freely in Your Body
https://taroiwamoto.com/thecourse?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=fear_of_movement_description_course

This is a guided somatic learning process for thoughtful, self-aware adults who are ready to move beyond chasing temporary relief and begin developing a different relationship with their body — one built through awareness, experience, connection, and greater choice.

Read my book

Your Body Is Not Broken: A Gentle Somatic Path to Moving with More Ease, Trust, and Freedom

A short Kindle book for anyone who is tired of treating their body like a problem to solve and wants a gentler place to begin.

https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GX363HMX

About Taro Iwamoto

I’m a nervous system movement coach helping adults who feel stuck in recurring pain, tension, bracing, stiffness, or fear of movement — even after trying many approaches — discover a gentler path toward more ease, trust, and freedom in their body.

My work isn’t about finding the perfect exercise or correcting everything that seems wrong.

It’s about helping you notice how your body has learned to organize movement and giving it experiences through which new possibilities can emerge.

videos.summary_source_text:
NEW Audi Q7: The ultimate SUV? Is the all-new Audi Q7 the ultimate 7-seat SUV?

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Mat’s flown over to France for his first drive of the all-new Audi Q7! 

It’s the third generation of Audi’s flagship 7-seater, but the question is, does it have what it takes to compete with class-leading competitors like the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS? Let’s take a closer look…

Starting with the design, the new Q7 has more road presence than the previous iteration. The car is slightly wider and taller than before, and up front you’ll find a wider, larger grille which is flanked on either side by Audi’s new stacked headlight design. There’s also a set of DRLs that can display a choice of different patterns within them. Along the side, the alloy sizes range from 20” to 23”, and the car here has black surrounds on the windows and black roof bars. Around the back, you’ll find a set of OLED tail lights, and amazingly, a pair of real exhaust pipes - no fakery here! 

Step inside and you’ll find a pretty luxurious interior, with the cabin of the Q7 dominated by a whole lot of screen action. The digital dials and infotainment screen are housed in the same curved design that stretches across the majority of the dash, while there’s also a separate passenger screen that comes as standard. Pretty much any surface on the inside is fitted with soft-touch materials, and the seats we have here are fitted with wool-effect material, which is lovely to touch. The seats also available with heated and cooled functionality. 

The Q7 we have here is fitted with a 3-litre V6 diesel engine that produces 299hp and 630Nm of torque. This power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox. It’s also fitted with mild-hybrid tech, and petrol and plug-in hybrid models will also be available. 

The entry-level Q7 starts from £81,665, with the range-topping model (as we have in this video) starting from £101,655. So is it worth it? And more importantly, would you choose it over a BMW X7? Let us know in the comments!

11.08.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Are The Avalanche and Cale Makar Disagreeing on Term? The Most Significant Goal in Team History. Have Cale Makar’s contract talks with the Colorado Avalanche hit a snag? Are term limits the real barrier to a new extension? With the NHL salary cap rising and stars like Connor Bedard and Leo Carlsson opting for shorter deals, Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson debate whether Makar should maximize his earnings or lock in security for the long haul. Will Joe Sakic and Avalanche management bend, or will Makar settle for fewer years to chase a bigger payday down the line?

The conversation heats up with a look at the most significant goals in Avalanche history—does Darren Helm’s game-winner against St. Louis rival Uwe Krupp’s Cup-winning overtime goal? Fans chime in with their picks, while franchise-altering moments like Patrick Roy’s fateful night in Montreal spark debate. videos.title: The ‘King of Sling’ Mac Boucher On Being A Self-Taught Pro + Golf Content Creation | Closed Course
videos.summary_source_text:
The ‘King of Sling’ Mac Boucher On Being A Self-Taught Pro + Golf Content Creation | Closed Course Welcome back to another episode of ‘Closed Course’ powered by Pins and Aces!

Blake and Erik are back for another great interview, catching up with former professional golfer and golf content creator, Mac Boucher!

Mac picked up a golf club for the first time at the age of 18, and is fully self-taught when it comes to his unique skill set. After a brain cyst forced him to give up all the sports he grew up playing, golf became his passion and number one priority. He worked with Sean Foley to perfect his game, and started playing professionally in Canada. His professional career slowed down in 2017, when he moved to New Zealand to become a teaching professional. During COVID, when teaching slowed down, he transitioned more into golf content creation, making all sorts of social media content around his unique golf game. After grinding to gain a significant following, Mac is now a well-known golf creator, and has one of the largest golf-based followings in all of Canada!

Mac and the guys discuss his journey to becoming a self-taught pro, how he broke into the realm of content creation, the increased crossover between professional athletes and golf, and all sorts of different events and tournaments that he has coming up in the near future. From the best golf courses in Canada, his biggest tips for golf content creation, and so much more, this is an awesome interview you won’t want to miss!

You can find Mac on Instagram, X, TikTok, and YouTube @macbouchergolf

Tune into ‘Closed Course’ Tuesdays at 6:00 A.M. for unforgettable interviews, golf convos, and more!

https://improve.shotcraftgolf.com/products/blue-brick/lp9_big_swing?utm_content=[youtube]&utm_medium=social

If you can't hit draws, it's not your swing plane it's actually your right elbow.

This video breaks down why your right arm gets "over the top" in transition, killing your window at impact and causing pulls and slices. You'll learn exactly where tour players position their trail elbow at impact and the simple one-handed drill to feel it yourself.

After watching, you'll know how to create the biggest possible "window" between your elbows at impact, get the club coming from the inside, and start compressing the ball for real draws instead of slices.

We used the Blue Brick as visual feedback to confirm the club is swinging from the inside while you groove the elbow position.

videos.title: Moving Punch Turn Challenge
videos.summary_source_text:
Moving Punch Turn Challenge The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

When it comes to working out with shoulder pain, I know that there are 7 exercises that are troublesome. Does that mean you should stop doing them altogether? Or is there something that can be done to mitigate the pain while still getting the benefits of the exercise? As a physical therapist and someone that has bad shoulders myself, I can tell you that avoiding these exercises altogether is not the solution.

The first exercise that could be a problem with shoulder pain is one you might not immediately think of and that's the pullup. In the case of a labrum tear, this can be one of the most aggravating exercises. The fix here is to depress your shoulders - create distance between your ears and your biceps as you hang from the bar. When you are lowering yourself down from the top of the pull-up, there are 2 things you need to do. The first is to slow yourself down as you descend. The second is to never disengage the packing of your shoulders throughout the rep. This will let you keep getting the benefits of the pullup without aggravating a compromised labrum.

The next troublesome exercise for a bum shoulder is an obvious one that, again, you shouldn't be skipping. That is the bench press. Most people experience shoulder pain or shoulder discomfort on the bench press when they use a barbell. That is because of the fixed arm position of the arms when using the bar. If you are going to use a barbell to bench press, then you will want to take a more narrow grip. This will help with elbow positioning in preventing you from flaring your arms out to the sides (incurring greater internal rotation) as well as activating the lats to stabilize the press. In many cases, I would say that if a barbell bench press is causing shoulder pain, then you're likely better off switching to dumbbells. This will allow freedom to tuck the elbows as much as needed to avoid shoulder pain. The key here is to go slow to create greater stability.

If there is one exercise you should skip altogether when it comes to working out with shoulder pain, it would be the upright row. It's just not a good exercise due to its ability to create shoulder problems in the first place (such as with impingement) and any benefits it has when it comes to shoulder growth can be mirrored by another, safer exercise. In this instance, simply opt to perform a dumbbell high pull instead. The added benefit of external rotation at the top of the rep will help prevent impingement and promote healthy shoulder mechanics.

We don't only have to focus on the upper body to find exercises that will be tough on a creaky shoulder. As a matter of fact, the king of leg exercises, the squat, can be a big problem if you don't have the right shoulder mobility. I'm specifically talking about the low bar squat, which requires a lot of shoulder external rotation to get into the proper position. However, we have some simple fixes so you can still squat without pain. If low bar squatting is what you want to do, try a wider grip for less shoulder mobility demand. Otherwise, you can switch to a high bar squat or a front squat, which will still have a heavy impact on your leg growth.

Now, I've heard time and time again that if you have bad shoulders, you shouldn't do dips. I disagree. I think you just need to pay attention to how you are performing the exercise. The first thing to take note of is that you should be taking the same tip from the pullups when it comes to depressing your shoulder blades - keep your shoulders back and down throughout the entire movement. On top of that, stick your chest out. A proud chest will make sure your chest is taking the brunt of the work instead of the shoulders. Don't think you need some extreme amount of stretch at the bottom of the rep either. Cut your depth a little short to where you are getting some stretch on the pecs without aggravating your shoulder pain.

Watch how Tommy Fleetwood extends his arms through the ball while keeping his head back — and how applying that same feel takes Sean from pulling everything to hitting his first draw. These are the same golf tips Eric uses at his schools to stop pull and fade patterns fast. If you leave this video without trying the wide arc follow through drill, you're leaving a draw and solid iron contact on the table.

• Why an out to in golf swing path causes pulls, fades, and poor iron contact — and how to fix it
• How arm bending through impact creates an out to in path and how arm extension creates an in to out swing
• The wide arc follow through drill: pushing the butt of the club away to improve golf swing path
• How forearm rotation in the golf swing squares the club face when swinging more from inside
• Why lead hand fingers under trail hand is the checkpoint for correct arm rotation through impact
• How Tommy Fleetwood uses arm extension and golf follow through to stay on plane through the ball
• The 4:00 drill for getting the club into the correct inside delivery position

David Carle & Red Wings Talk | Morning Cuppa Hockey On this summer edition of Morning Cuppa Hockey, Jonny Lazarus and Colby Cohen are joined by Denver Pioneers head coach David Carle for a wide-ranging conversation on the future of college hockey. Carle discusses constantly being linked to NHL coaching openings, why he remains committed to Denver, how he handles those rumours with his players and administration, and the family culture the Pioneers have built. They dive into Carle’s proposal to overhaul the NCAA recruiting calendar, age-based eligibility changes, the ideal number of games for a college hockey season, experimenting with Thursday and Friday games, growing hockey in the United States through the NCAA, his own future in the sport, and how Denver continues to recruit and develop elite talent. After the interview, Jonny and Colby break down Denver’s player development and sports science model, the problems with recruiting players too young, whether college hockey needs a commissioner, the disappearance of NHL bridge deals and how NIL and revenue sharing could impact player decisions, before closing with the latest on Dylan Larkin’s trade situation and what comes next for the Detroit Red Wings.
